en: to be forced; to be pressured; to be coerced

examples.en: I was forced to apologize and it made me feel bad.

examples.ko: 굴복을 강요받은 직원이 결국 회사를 그만두었어요.
examples.en: The employee who was pressured to give in finally quit the company.

examples.ko: 아이들은 공부를 너무 강요받으면 흥미를 잃어요.
examples.en: Children lose interest if they are pushed too hard to study.

examples.ko: 저는 한 번도 결혼을 강요받은 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never been pressured to get married.
A friend pressured me to lend him money.
If you feel pressured, it's okay to refuse.

explain: '강요하다'의 반대편에서 하는 말이에요. 'A에게 B를 강요받다'처럼 써요. '강요당하다'도 비슷한데, '-당하다'는 억울하고 힘든 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I was forced to work against my will.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강요받다'와 비슷하지만 더 억울하고 힘든 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 강요받다 but with a stronger feeling of unfairness.

phrases.en: I decided myself without being forced by anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 마음대로 선택했다는 뜻으로 부정형을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, meaning you chose freely.

phrases.en: I feel pressured, so I don't like it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분을 말할 때 '느낌'과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 느낌 to describe how you feel.

explain_en: It describes the side that receives what '강요하다' (to force) does. It is used like 'A에게 B를 강요받다'. '강요당하다' is similar, but '-당하다' feels more unfair and painful.

examples.ko: 회사의 비리를 알린 고발자가 보호를 받고 있어요.
examples.en: The whistle-blower who exposed the company's corruption is being protected.
The name of the whistle-blower was not made public.
He found courage and became a whistle-blower.
They say we need a law that protects whistle-blowers.
The accuser's and the accused's stories are different.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 고발자가 직접 기자회견을 했어요.
examples.en: The whistle-blower from the news held a press conference in person.

explain: 회사나 조직 안의 잘못을 알리는 사람은 '내부 고발자'라고 해요. 법에서는 피해자가 직접 하면 '고소', 제3자도 할 수 있는 신고를 '고발'이라고 구분해요.

phrases.en: That employee is the company's whistle-blower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직 안에서 잘못을 알린 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who exposed wrongdoing from inside an organization.

phrases.en: The law must protect whistle-blowers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도나 법에 관한 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about laws and systems.

phrases.en: He found the courage and became a whistle-blower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못을 알리는 입장이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means he took the position of reporting wrongdoing.

explain_en: Someone who exposes wrongdoing inside a company or organization is called an '내부 고발자'. In law, a victim filing is '고소', while '고발' is a report that a third party can also make.

examples.en: I have to submit documents to the office of education.

examples.ko: 시 교육청에서 새 소식을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The city office of education shared some news.
The education office building is next to city hall.
The office of education supports school events.
I looked up our local education office's website.
The teacher went to a training session at the education office.

explain: '교육부'는 나라 전체의 교육을 맡고, '교육청'은 시·도 단위로 학교를 관리해요. 학교 일은 학교를 거쳐 교육청에 올라가요. '서울시교육청'처럼 지역 이름을 앞에 붙여요.

phrases.en: I called the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어느 지역의 교육청인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a region name first to say which region's office it is.

phrases.en: Please ask the office of education for details.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 일에 대해 질문할 때 '에 문의하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 문의하다' to ask questions about school matters.
phrases.en_equiv: to inquire at the education office

phrases.en: The Ministry of Education handles education for the whole country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '교육부'는 나라 전체를 맡고, '교육청'은 시·도 단위를 맡아요.
phrases.nuance_en: '교육부' covers the whole country; '교육청' covers a city or province.

explain_en: '교육부' handles education for the whole country, while a '교육청' manages the schools of a city or province. School matters go up through the school to the 교육청. The region name goes in front, as in '서울시교육청'.

examples.en: The Supreme Court is in Seocho-gu, Seoul.
This case went all the way to the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court ruling came out today.
The appeal was dismissed, so they appealed to the Supreme Court.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 대법원 앞에 모인 사람들을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw on the news the people gathered in front of the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court will make the final decision.

explain: 한국의 법원은 지방법원, 고등법원, 대법원 순서로 올라가요. 대법원이 가장 높아서 여기서 나온 판결이 마지막이에요. 책임자는 '대법원장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The Chief Justice announced the ruling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대법원의 책임자를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The title for the head of the Supreme Court.

phrases.en: The Supreme Court ruling came out yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 마지막 판결을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for the final ruling.

phrases.en: The final decision is made at the Supreme Court.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'와 함께 써서 대법원이 결정하는 장소·주체임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 에서 to show the Supreme Court as the place or body of decision.
phrases.en_equiv: to decide at the Supreme Court

explain_en: Korean courts go up in order: '지방법원' (district court), '고등법원' (high court), then '대법원'. It is the highest, so its ruling is final. Its head is called the '대법원장' (chief justice).

en: to be introduced (adopted: a system, technology, policy)

examples.en: The new system will be introduced next week.
This system was introduced last year.
It's a method that was brought in from overseas.
Once self-checkout is introduced, it'll be more convenient.
I watched the process of the new technology being introduced.
It's a service that hasn't been introduced yet.

explain: 제도, 기술, 기계처럼 밖에서 들여와 쓰기 시작하는 것에 써요. 사람을 소개하는 '소개하다'와는 달라요. 보통 회사나 나라 차원의 이야기라 뉴스나 업무 대화에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The system introduced this year is very convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.example: 새 기술이 여러 회사에 도입되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The new technology is being introduced at many companies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 퍼지고 있는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is in the process of spreading.

phrases.example: 다음 달부터 이 규칙이 새로 도입돼요.
phrases.en: This rule will be newly introduced starting next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 들여오는 것을 강조할 때 '새로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 새로 to stress that something is being brought in for the first time.

explain_en: Use it for systems, technologies, or machines that are brought in from outside and begin to be used. It is different from 소개하다, which is for introducing people. It usually concerns companies or countries, so you hear it in news and work talk.

examples.en: My great-grandfather was someone who took part in the independence movement.

examples.ko: 독립운동가의 후손들이 기념식에 초대돼 감사패를 받았어요.
examples.en: Descendants of independence activists were invited to the ceremony and received plaques of appreciation.
The liberation of 1945 came after a long independence movement.
I learned the history of the independence movement at school.

examples.ko: 독립운동 때문에 감옥에 간 분들도 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people went to prison because of the independence movement.
The museum is exhibiting materials on the independence movement.

explain: 한국에서는 일제강점기에 나라를 되찾으려 한 활동을 가리킬 때 가장 많이 써요. 그 일을 한 사람은 '독립운동가'라고 해요. 같은 맥락에서 '광복'이나 '3·1 운동'도 함께 배워요.

phrases.en: I read the story of an independence activist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 한 '사람'을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who took part in the movement.

phrases.en: Many people took part in the independence movement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 활동에 함께했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means joining in the activity.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in the independence movement

phrases.en: I learned the history of the independence movement at school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 책에서 배우는 내용을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what you study in class or books.

explain_en: In Korea this most often refers to the activities to regain the country during the Japanese colonial period. A person who took part is called a '독립운동가'. In the same context you also learn '광복' (liberation) and the '3·1 Movement'.

examples.en: The media covered that accident widely.

examples.ko: 매스컴이 유명한 사람의 이야기를 자주 보도해요.
examples.en: The media often reports stories about famous people.
I learned the news through the media.
The influence of the media is growing.
It is a shop famous enough to appear in the media.
Do not trust media reports too much.

explain: 신문과 방송을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 '매스컴' 말고 '언론'이나 '미디어'라는 말도 써요. '매스컴을 타다'는 방송이나 신문에 나온다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 매스컴을 타고 나서 손님이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: get media coverage
phrases.nuance_ko: 방송이나 신문에 소개되어 널리 알려진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is introduced on TV or in newspapers and becomes widely known.

explain_en: To refer to newspapers and broadcasts together, people also say '언론' or '미디어' instead of '매스컴'. The phrase '매스컴을 타다' is used for getting into the news or on TV.

examples.en: People from the cultural world gathered at the event.
The cultural community was shocked by this incident.
That actor is a respected figure in the cultural field.
I read cultural news in the culture section of the newspaper.
That person has led the cultural field for a long time.
The reaction of the cultural community was mostly positive.

explain: 문화·예술 일을 하는 사람들과 그 분야 전체를 묶어서 말할 때 써요. '정치계', '연예계'처럼 '-계'가 붙은 말이고, 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: One hundred figures from the cultural community issued a statement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화·예술 분야에서 알려진 사람들을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to well-known people in the culture and arts fields.

phrases.en: I want to work in the cultural field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 일하는 분야를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a job or the field someone works in.
phrases.en_equiv: to work in the cultural field

phrases.en: I read cultural news in the newspaper today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 신문의 문화 분야 기사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for news in the culture section of a paper or broadcast.

explain_en: It refers to the people and the whole field of culture and the arts together. Like '정치계' (political world) and '연예계' (entertainment world), it uses '-계' and often appears in news and articles.

en: to be shot; to be launched (gun, rocket, missile)

examples.en: The rocket is launched today.
The satellite was launched yesterday.
Fireworks were shot into the sky.

examples.ko: 발사된 우주선이 지구 둘레를 돌고 있어요.
examples.en: The launched spacecraft is orbiting the Earth.
A launch can happen only when the weather is good.
It is a rocket that has not been launched yet.

explain: 로켓, 우주선, 불꽃놀이 같은 것이 공중으로 쏘아 올려지는 것이 주어예요. 쏘는 사람이 주어면 '발사하다', 쏘아지는 것이 주어면 '발사되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The rocket is scheduled to be launched tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 계획을 알릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce a future plan.

phrases.en: It could not be launched because the weather was bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 못하다'로 하고 싶었지만 안 됐다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 못하다' shows it was expected but could not happen.

phrases.en: As soon as the rocket was launched, it disappeared into the clouds.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-자마자'는 앞 일이 끝나고 바로 다음 일이 일어난다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-자마자' means the next thing happens right after the first.
phrases.en_equiv: as soon as it is launched

explain_en: The subject is the thing being shot up into the air, such as a rocket, a spacecraft or fireworks. If the subject is the one firing it, use '발사하다'. If the subject is the thing being fired, use '발사되다'.

en: to come into effect; to bring into force

examples.en: The new law takes effect from next month.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 맺은 조약이 오늘 발효했어요.
examples.en: The treaty between the two countries came into force today.

examples.ko: 비상 경보가 발효하면 모두 대피해야 해요.
examples.en: When the emergency alert is in effect, everyone has to evacuate.

examples.ko: 계약이 발효하기 전에 내용을 다시 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: Read the contract again before it takes effect.

examples.ko: 이 규정은 발효한 지 이미 오 년이 되었어요.
examples.en: This rule has already been in force for five years.

examples.ko: 협정이 발효할 날짜가 아직 정해지지 않았어요.
examples.en: The date when the agreement takes effect has not been set yet.

explain: 법, 조약, 계약처럼 공식적인 약속이 실제로 효력을 가지기 시작할 때 써요. 같은 소리의 '발효'는 김치나 된장이 익는다는 뜻의 다른 말이라 문맥으로 구별해요. '시행하다'는 법을 실제로 실시한다는 뜻이고, '발효하다'는 효력이 생기는 때를 말해요.

phrases.en: The new rule takes effect from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발효하다'와 뜻은 같지만, 법이나 조약이 주어일 때는 '발효되다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It has the same meaning as '발효하다', but '발효되다' is used more often when a law or treaty is the subject.

phrases.en: Once you sign the contract, it takes effect.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발효하다'와 뜻이 같은 쉬운 말이고, 일상에서 풀어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase with the same meaning as '발효하다', used when explaining things in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 이 조약은 다음 달에 발효될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: This treaty is scheduled to take effect next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 시작하지 않았지만 곧 효력이 생길 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used often in the news when something has not started yet but will take effect soon.

explain_en: Used when a law, treaty or contract starts to have effect. There is a different word with the same sound, 발효, meaning fermentation of kimchi or soybean paste, so use context to tell them apart. 시행하다 is putting a law into practice, while 발효하다 is the point at which it becomes valid.

examples.en: The celebrity's scandal was in the news.
That politician stepped down because of the scandal.

examples.ko: 스캔들에 대해 아무 말도 안 했어요.
examples.en: He said nothing about the scandal.
The company tried to hide the scandal.
A scandal spreads by word of mouth quickly.
He is a person who became famous through a scandal.

explain: '스캔들이 나다', '스캔들에 휘말리다'처럼 말해요. 뉴스나 글에서는 '추문'이라는 어려운 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: That actor is having a hard time because of a scandal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스캔들이 세상에 알려졌다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a scandal became known to the public.

phrases.en: That singer got caught up in a scandal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않게 스캔들에 얽혔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gets tangled in a scandal.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught up in a scandal

phrases.en: A scandal article was posted online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스캔들을 다룬 뉴스를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a news article about a scandal.

explain_en: People say 'seukaendeuri nada' (a scandal breaks out) and 'seukaendeure hwimallida' (get caught up in a scandal). In news and writing, a harder word, 'chumun', also exists.

examples.en: A hiker went missing in the mountains yesterday.
I saw news that a child had gone missing.
I'm looking for a missing puppy.
When the ship went missing at sea, the rescue team was sent out.
He was found three days after he went missing.
If a family member goes missing, you must report it to the police.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 사라져서 있는 곳을 알 수 없을 때 써요. 물건에는 '분실되다'나 '잃어버리다'를 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 무거운 말이라서 일상에서 가볍게 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: They are looking for the missing child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 사라진 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, pointing to the person who went missing.

phrases.en: The family filed a missing person report at the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사라진 사람을 경찰에 알릴 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reporting a missing person to the police.

phrases.en: They say a person went missing in the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스 같은 말을 전해 줄 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form for passing on what you heard, such as from the news.

explain_en: It is used when a person or animal has vanished and nobody knows where they are. For objects, use 분실되다 or 잃어버리다. It is a heavy word heard in the news, so it is not used lightly in daily talk.

examples.ko: 내일 태풍이 올 거라고 미리 예고됐어요.
examples.en: It was announced in advance that a typhoon would hit tomorrow.

examples.ko: 새 드라마의 첫 방송이 예고되고 있어요.
examples.en: The first episode of the new drama is being previewed.

examples.ko: 정전이 예고된 날에는 미리 휴대폰을 충전해 둬요.
examples.en: On days when a power outage is announced, I charge my phone ahead of time.

examples.ko: 회사에 큰 변화가 예고돼서 다들 긴장했어요.
examples.en: A big change at the company was announced, so everyone got nervous.

examples.ko: 눈이 온다고 예고될 때마다 일찍 퇴근해요.
examples.en: Whenever snow is forecast, I leave work early.
The water cut was announced in advance, but I didn't know.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '미리 알려 주다'를 더 자주 써요. '예고되다'는 뉴스, 방송, 공지에서 '정전이 예고되다'처럼 나와요. 알리는 쪽은 '예고하다', 알려지는 일은 '예고되다'예요.

phrases.en: The power outage was announced in advance, so I prepared.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예고된'은 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 공지나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form modifies a noun after it. It is common in notices and news.

phrases.en: That was not announced in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 생긴 일을 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used for something that happened suddenly, without warning.

phrases.example: 내일 정전이 있다고 미리 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: They told us in advance that there will be a power outage tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '예고되다'보다 이 말이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday conversation this sounds much more natural than 예고되다.
phrases.en_equiv: to let someone know in advance

explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '미리 알려 주다' more often. '예고되다' shows up in news, broadcasts and notices, as in '정전이 예고되다'. The one announcing uses '예고하다'; the thing announced is '예고되다'.

examples.en: Next year's economy is forecast to improve.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 비가 올 것으로 전망됐어요.
examples.en: Rain was forecast for this weekend.

examples.ko: 고객이 더 늘어날 것으로 전망되고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of customers is expected to grow further.

examples.ko: 올해 매출은 크게 오를 것으로 전망된대요.
examples.en: They say sales are projected to rise sharply this year.
It is a situation where interest rates are expected to fall.
It was a time when the economy was forecast to recover.

explain: '~을 것으로 전망돼요'처럼 뉴스에서 앞일을 예상할 때 써요. 내가 예상하면 '전망하다', 그렇게 예상된다고 전할 때는 '전망되다'예요. 가까운 말로 '예상되다'가 있어요.

phrases.example: 전문가들은 내년에 물가가 오를 것으로 전망해요.
phrases.en: Experts predict prices will rise next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 앞일을 예상한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person makes a prediction.

phrases.en: Rain is expected tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 가깝고, 뉴스 말고 일상에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning and also usable in daily life, not just news.

phrases.example: 올해 경기가 좋아질 것으로 전망되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The economy is expected to improve this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 그렇게 예상되는 중이라는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests that this outlook still holds right now.

explain_en: News uses '~을 것으로 전망돼요' to talk about the future. 'Jeonmanghada' is when someone predicts, and 'jeonmangdoeda' reports that something is predicted. '예상되다' is a close word.

examples.en: They caught the criminal thanks to a citizen's tip.
Many tips came in to the TV station.

examples.ko: 저는 이상한 일을 보고 바로 제보를 했어요.
examples.en: I saw something strange and reported it right away.
They take news tips by phone or email.
It was an anonymous tip, so I do not know who sent it.

examples.ko: 제보 덕분에 사고 원인을 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the tip, we learned the cause of the accident.

explain: '제보'는 뉴스, 경찰, 회사 같은 곳에 사건이나 정보를 알려 주는 일이에요. 친구에게 알려 주는 것은 '알려 주다'이고, '제보'는 공적인 곳에 보내는 느낌이에요. 보통 '제보를 받다', '제보가 들어오다'처럼 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The police received a tip from a citizen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알려 주는 정보를 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pair, from the side receiving the information.

phrases.en: The informant's name is secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정보를 알려 준 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who gave the information.

phrases.en: I made a tip-off call to the TV station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이나 정보를 알리려고 거는 전화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phone call made to report an event or information.

explain_en: 제보 is telling news, police or a company about an incident or information. Telling a friend is 알려 주다, while 제보 is directed to an official place. It often goes with 제보를 받다 or 제보가 들어오다.

examples.ko: 도로에 큰 구멍이 있어서 시청에 제보했어요.
examples.en: There was a big hole in the road, so I reported it to city hall.

examples.ko: 사고를 본 사람은 경찰에 제보해 주세요.
examples.en: If you saw the accident, please tell the police.

examples.ko: 쓰레기를 몰래 버리는 사람을 구청에 제보할 거예요.
examples.en: I will report the person secretly dumping trash to the district office.
Please tell me how to send a tip to the TV station.

examples.ko: 직원이 회사의 문제를 기자에게 제보한 일이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a case where an employee tipped a reporter about the company's problem.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 위험한 일을 보면 시청에 제보하세요.
examples.en: If you see something dangerous at a construction site, report it to the city hall.

explain: '제보하다'는 경찰, 방송국, 구청처럼 공적인 곳에 알리는 말이에요. 개인에게 알릴 때는 '알려 주다'를 쓰고, 나쁜 일을 알릴 때는 '신고하다'가 더 가까워요. '신고하다'는 법적으로 알리는 느낌이고 '제보하다'는 정보를 준다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I tipped off the police about the accident site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 알렸다는 말로, 신고한 일을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, used when talking about something you reported.

phrases.en: If you report a problem, the district office checks it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알린 뒤에 어떤 일이 생기는지 조건으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what happens after you report something.

phrases.en: I'll report what I saw to the TV station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 알리겠다고 말할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you will report something.

explain_en: 제보하다 is telling a public place such as the police, a TV station or a district office. For a person you use 알려 주다, and for reporting wrongdoing 신고하다 is closer. 신고하다 feels legal, while 제보하다 is about giving information.

examples.en: The party leadership announced its position today.
The new leadership is made up of young people.
The student council leadership started talking with the school.
Everyone agreed to follow the leadership's decision.
The union leaders and the company met again.
Some suggested changing the leadership.

explain: 지도부는 정당, 노조, 학생회처럼 조직을 이끄는 사람들 전체를 말해요. 한 사람은 '지도자', 회사에서는 '경영진'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서 '당 지도부'로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The union leadership met with the company's CEO.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노동조합을 이끄는 사람들 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for all the people who lead a labor union.

phrases.en: The leadership was replaced after the election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직을 이끄는 사람들이 새로 바뀔 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the people leading an organization are replaced.

phrases.en: The management announced a new plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정당이나 노조가 아니라 회사를 이끄는 사람들은 '경영진'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people who lead a company, not a party or union, use 경영진.

explain_en: 지도부 refers to the whole group of people leading an organization such as a party, union or student council. One person is a 지도자 (leader), and in companies the group is called 경영진 (management). The news often says '당 지도부' (party leadership).

en: to be passed; to go through (a bill, test, inspection)

examples.en: My proposal was approved in the meeting.
That law has to be passed in the National Assembly.
If the document screening is passed, you'll get a call.
We only sell products that have passed inspection.

examples.ko: 계획서가 통과되지 않아서 다시 써야 해요.
examples.en: The plan wasn't approved, so I have to rewrite it.
I'm waiting until my application is approved.

explain: 심사, 검사, 투표 같은 단계를 무사히 넘어 인정받았다는 뜻이에요. 내가 시험에 붙을 때는 '통과하다'나 '합격하다'를 써요. 통과되다는 안건이나 서류처럼 사물이 주어일 때 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: My documents didn't pass the review.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심사를 넘지 못했다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it did not get past the review.

phrases.en: Please check the proposal that was passed yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I'm relieved the inspection passed without trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 없이 넘었을 때 '무사히'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 무사히 when something got through without problems.

explain_en: It means getting through a review, inspection, or vote and being accepted. When you yourself pass an exam, use 통과하다 or 합격하다. 통과되다 is natural when the subject is a thing like a proposal or document.

examples.en: The police called in the suspect yesterday and questioned him.
The suspect said from the start that he had done nothing wrong.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 피의자 얼굴은 보여 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: The news did not show the suspect's face.

examples.ko: 변호사가 피의자와 두 시간 동안 이야기했어요.
examples.en: The lawyer talked with the suspect for two hours.
The suspect in the case was caught last night.
The suspect's family cried in front of the reporters.

explain: 피의자는 경찰이나 검찰이 조사하는 단계의 사람이고, 재판에 넘겨지면 '피고인'이라고 불러요. 뉴스에서는 자주 들리지만 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: There will be a suspect interrogation at the police station tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 덩어리 표현으로, 경찰이 조사하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common set phrase in the news for the police questioning a suspect.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 사고 때문에 피의자로 조사받았어요.
phrases.en: He was investigated as a suspect because of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-로 조사받다'를 붙여 어떤 신분으로 조사받는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-로 조사받다' tells in what status someone is being investigated.
phrases.en_equiv: to be questioned as a suspect

phrases.en: He went to the police station as a suspect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건에서 그 사람의 법적인 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's legal position in a case.

explain_en: 피의자 is the person under investigation by police or prosecutors; once the case goes to trial the person is called 피고인. You hear it often in the news but almost never in everyday talk.
